newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower across the board on Thursday in what traders termed a much-needed correction.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.49 percent, or 4.37 points, to 288.26 on a very heavy all-share turnover of 207 million shekels against 260 million shekels on Monday, the last day of trading before the Jewish holiday of Shavuot.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.50 percent lower at 296.20.

"What we saw today was aggressive profit-taking after the market made a very big move upward during the last two months. It's about time for a technical correction. The market can not go in just one direction," said Ron Weisberg of IBI Investment House.

"This is a healthy consolidation," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim. "The market rose very fast in a short time because share prices were cheap. But now the market is very fragile and, despite the fact that the trend is still positive, the market will rise at a much slower pace."
He said the correction might continue several more days.
Weisberg added that activity is expected to be relatively low on Sunday ahead of the release of May consumer price index (CPI).
"On Monday it's a new ball game. If the figure is at the lower range of expectations the probability for a rate cut is high," he said.
The Bank of Israel is scheduled to announce its July monetary programme, including interest rates, on June 23. The base rate has been unchanged at 13.9 percent since the end of February.

The CPI, to be released after the end of the trading day on Sunday, is expected to show a rise of 0.7 to 0.9 percent against an increase of 0.7 percent in April. The Hapoalim trader said a CPI of less than 0.8 percent would be seen as a positive indicator.
"This might give the market fuel for another rise although the market needs to slow down," he said.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which fell 1.25 percent to 535 agorot on turnover of 12.8 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which lost 1.0 percent to 811 agorot on volume of 12.4 million shekels; and Koor Industries, which gained 1.0 percent to 32,193 agorot on volume of 10 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
